item.title: Drupal Security Team Warns Second RCE Flaw Is Actively Exploited
item.description:
Drupal Security Team Warns Second RCE Flaw Is Actively Exploited

The Drupal security team announced that attackers are exploiting a second critical vulnerability that allows them to breach and hijack unpatched websites. This follows the recent patching of a remote code execution flaw known as CVE-2026-132165, or Fail2Install, which allowed anonymous users to take over vulnerable sites by abusing the Drupal installer. An update to the original security advisory warned that threat actors began exploiting the initial flaw one day after patches were released.

🧩 The New Vulnerability

The new security issue, tracked as CVE-2026-136716, was patched one week after the initial release. It addresses attack vectors that were left unpatched in the previous advisory and also enables attackers to hijack vulnerable Drupal sites. While most installations are covered by the patch, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover, including production environments.

🔍 Detection Challenges

According to Drupal, it is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state. Furthermore, sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state. The team emphasized that this issue is being exploited in the wild, and any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.

⚙️ Recommended Actions

Drupal has warned users that any unsecured website may have been compromised and advised administrators to ensure the user 1 email address is one they control, considering a reset if necessary. Site logs should be checked for unauthorized access, with a focus on unexpected changes to or by the user 1 account.

For those who cannot immediately upgrade to Drupal 10.6.23, 11.3.23, or 11.4.14, the following mitigation is recommended:

  • Secure the installer on all new and existing sites by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file in the web root.
  • Follow the provided guide if evidence suggests the site may have been compromised.

💡 Broader Context

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged six Drupal security flaws as being abused in the wild since November 2021. Two of these flaws have also been exploited in ransomware attacks.

#Drupal #Security #CVE-2026-136716 #WebSecurity #VulnerabilityManagement

Source: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks

item.title: SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository
item.description:
SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository

SafeLine has newly appeared as a top-ranked GitHub trending repository for Go projects, establishing itself as a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) designed to protect web applications from attacks and exploits.

🔍 Overview

SafeLine is a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect web apps from attacks and exploits. A web application firewall helps protect web apps by filtering and monitoring HTTP traffic between a web application and the Internet.

🧩 How it Works

Unlike a proxy server that protects a client machine’s identity, a WAF operates as a reverse-proxy, shielding the server by routing client requests through the firewall before reaching the server. A WAF protects web apps by filtering, monitoring, and blocking malicious HTTP/S traffic while preventing unauthorized data from leaving the application. This is achieved through policies that distinguish between malicious and safe traffic.

⚙️ Key Details

SafeLine’s core capabilities include:

Capability Description
Block Web Attacks Defends against SQL injection, XSS, code injection, os command injection, CRLF injection, XXE, SSRF, path traversal, and other web attacks
Rate Limiting Thwarts DoS attacks, bruteforce attempts, traffic surges, and abuse by throttling excessive traffic
Anti-Bot Challenge Blocks bots and crawlers while allowing human users through challenge mechanisms
Authentication Challenge Requires password entry for visitors when enabled, blocking unauthenticated access
Dynamic Protection Dynamically encrypts HTML and JavaScript code with each visit to the web server

Additional features include defenses for web attacks, proactive bot abuse defense, HTML & JS code encryption, IP-based rate limiting, and Web Access Control List.

🚀 Availability

SafeLine has achieved significant recognition on GitHub:

  • #1 GitHub Trending Repository
  • #1 Go Repository of the Day
  • #1 Go Repository of the Week
  • #9 Go Repository of the Month

💡 Why It Matters

The rise of SafeLine highlights growing community interest in self-hosted, open-source security solutions for web application protection, offering organizations an auditable alternative to commercial WAF offerings.

#WAF #cybersecurity #GoLang #GitHub #WebSecurity

Source: chaitin/SafeLine

item.title: AWS WAF Introduces New Security Analytics Dashboard
item.description:
AWS WAF Introduces New Security Analytics Dashboard

AWS has introduced a new security analytics dashboard for AWS WAF, providing a single global page to investigate traffic across all protection packs (web ACLs), Regional resources, and Amazon CloudFront distributions. This update builds on the 2024 traffic overview dashboard by offering a consolidated view that helps users act on findings faster.

🔍 Overview

The new dashboard is designed to help users investigate and contain threats faster while reducing false positives that block real customers. Key aspects of the update include:

  • A single global page for investigating traffic across all protection packs (web ACLs).
  • Coverage of Regional resources and Amazon CloudFront distributions.
  • No need to build or maintain a custom log analytics pipeline.
  • Built on full-fidelity request data rather than samples.
  • Two primary use cases demonstrated: investigating a traffic spike and tuning rules to reduce false positives.

🧩 How It Works

To access the dashboard, users navigate to the AWS WAF console and select “Security analytics” in the navigation pane. The interface allows users to narrow the view to specific protection packs and set time ranges.

  • Global View: The dashboard displays request data across all protection packs in the account. Selecting “All protection packs” shows a comprehensive view.
  • Traffic Breakdown: The top of the page shows total requests split by action: Allow, Block, CAPTCHA, and Challenge.
  • Charts and Widgets: The “Requests chart” visualizes traffic changes over time, while widgets below display top values for specific dimensions. Users can split the Requests chart by dimensions such as Host, Rule triggered, Country, or JA4.
  • Host Grouping: Grouping or filtering by Host identifies which domains are under attack or experiencing spikes, even when a single protection pack protects multiple domains or a domain spans several protection packs.
  • Labels and Detections: AWS Managed Rules add labels (e.g., Bot Control categories, verification status, and signals like non_browser_user_agent). Users can also create custom labels. Because labels are recorded even when a rule is set to count-only, filtering by a label shows what a rule detected across all protection packs without changing how traffic is handled.
  • Filters and Actions: Filters apply to the entire dashboard, updating the action split, Requests chart, widgets, and request list. Users can select any value in a widget to focus on it, remove it, or block it.
  • Request Details: For individual requests, the dashboard displays HTTP fields such as host, path, headers, user agent, and JA4 fingerprint. It also shows which detections and labels matched and whether each action was enforced or only counted.

⚙️ Key Details

Previously, accessing this level of detail required working from a limited sample of requests or setting up and querying custom AWS WAF logs. The new dashboard makes this data available directly. Additionally, the current dashboard view is saved in the user’s browser.

💡 Why It Matters

This tool allows security teams to move from reactive log analysis to proactive investigation and containment. By providing full-fidelity data without the overhead of maintaining custom pipelines, organizations can more effectively tune their rules to minimize false positives and protect their infrastructure.

#AWS #WAF #WebSecurity #CloudSecurity #DataAnalytics

Source: Introducing the new AWS WAF security analytics dashboard | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Shannon: Open-Source AI Pentester for Web Applications
item.description:
Shannon: Open-Source AI Pentester for Web Applications

Shannon, an autonomous AI pentester for web applications and APIs developed by Keygraph, has been released as an open-source agent that can be run locally from the command line.

🔍 Overview

  • Shannon is an autonomous AI pentester for web applications and APIs.
  • It analyzes source code to identify attack vectors and executes real exploits to prove vulnerabilities before they reach production.
  • It is developed by Keygraph.

🧩 How it works

  • Shannon analyzes the web application’s source code to identify potential attack vectors.
  • It then uses browser automation and command-line tools to execute real exploits against the running application and its APIs.
  • Only vulnerabilities with a working proof-of-concept are included in the final report. The policy is “No exploit, no report.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Shannon is open-source and runs locally from the command line.
  • The same Shannon agent also powers Keygraph’s commercial editions: Pro and Enterprise.

🚀 Availability

  • The repository is Shannon: the full open-source agent, run locally from your command line.

💡 Why it matters

  • By requiring a working exploit before reporting, Shannon ensures that only proven vulnerabilities are documented, reducing false positives and providing actionable results.

#AI #pentesting #cybersecurity #opensource #websecurity #AIagents

Source: KeygraphHQ/shannon

item.title: University of Notre Dame Hosts AI Coding Assistant Security Workshop
item.description:
University of Notre Dame Hosts AI Coding Assistant Security Workshop

On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the AI Collaborative Programming group offered a virtual, hands‑on workshop where participants put AI coding assistants to the test in a web‑application security sandbox.

🔍 Overview

  • Date & Time: Thursday, October 8, 2026, 1:00 pm – 2:00 pm
  • Format: Virtual (250I Hesburgh Library link)
  • Goal: Identify and patch common security flaws using AI‑assisted tools while maintaining strict human oversight.

🛠️ Workshop Content

  • Work with AI tools such as GitHub Copilot or VS Code alongside an OWASP Juice Shop instance.
  • Follow a human‑in‑the‑loop workflow:
    • Isolate a vulnerability.
    • Create a Git branch.
    • Prompt the AI for a secure fix.
    • Verify the patch against insecure defaults.
    • Write clean PR documentation.
  • Learn to:
    • Critique AI‑generated code.
    • Spot dangerous hallucinations.
    • Maintain rigorous developer oversight.

👥 Presenters & Audience

Name Role
Rob Wieck Senior Research Software Engineer / Product Owner, AI Enablement
Julie Vecchio Interim Co‑Director, Navari Family Center for Digital Scholarship
  • Open to: Undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, staff, and postdocs.

📅 Details

  • Part of a series offered by the AI Collaborative Programming group, a partnership between Hesburgh Libraries, ND Learning, and the Office of Information Technology.
  • Location for the virtual session: 250I Hesburgh Library.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates practical ways to integrate AI coding assistants into secure software development.
  • Emphasizes the importance of human review to mitigate AI‑generated errors.
  • Provides a reproducible sandbox for learning secure coding practices.

#AI #CodingAssistants #WebSecurity #Workshop

Source: AI Masterclass: Developer Hands-On With AI-Assisted Coding Tools and OWASP Juice Shop
